notes: "Here is the kind of slide this talk is about: one real result. The structure is PDB entry 1BNA, the Dickerson–Drew DNA dodecamer, drawn from its deposited coordinates; chain A is green, chain B ochre. For each of the twelve base pairs we measured the distance between the paired C1-prime atoms. The plot is a Matplotlib figure drawn from the CSV by a short script kept in this project, at the size it appears on the slide. If a value or a label needs to change, you change the data or the script and draw the figure again; nobody retouches pixels, and nobody retypes numbers into a slide chart. The axis deliberately does not start at zero, so the geometric variation is visible. Be careful about what it says: these are twelve positions in a single crystal structure. They are not replicates and carry no error bars. The shortest distance is at pair 7, a T–A pair in the central AATT region; the longest at pair 12, a terminal G–C pair.\n\nMethod: Euclidean distance between C1′ atoms, chain A residues 1–12 ascending paired with chain B residues 24–13 descending. Values in sources/independent-20261111/science/paired-c1-distances.csv, computed from the RCSB file by generate_1bna.py; figure by plot_c1_distances.py (PNG, SVG and PDF).\n\nSource: RCSB PDB 1BNA, https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1BNA; structure DOI 10.2210/pdb1BNA/pdb. Drew HR, Wing RM, Takano T, Broka C, Tanaka S, Itakura K, Dickerson RE. PNAS 78 (1981) 2179–2183, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.78.4.2179."

designIntent.purpose: Show the twelve measured C1′–C1′ distances beside the structure they were measured in.
keep: Labelled non-zero y-axis, units in Å
No replicate, error-bar or trend claims
Figure regenerated by plot_c1_distances.py, never retouched
designIntent.requestedChange: Replace the in-slide chart with a Matplotlib figure drawn from paired-c1-distances.csv by plot_c1_distances.py; values, axis range, citation and the extremes table unchanged.
